t: Deny Yourself and Follow the Lord to Find True Life
v: Then Jesus said to his disciples, “If anyone desires to come after me, let him deny himself, take up his cross, and follow me.
For whoever desires to save his life will lose it, and whoever will lose his life for my sake will find it.
For what will it profit a man if he gains the whole world and forfeits his life? Or what will a man give in exchange for his life?
For the Son of Man will come in the glory of his Father with his angels, and then he will give to everyone according to his deeds.
Most certainly I tell you, there are some standing here who will in no way taste of death until they see the Son of Man coming in his Kingdom.”
b: Jesus said to his disciples, “If anyone desires to come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me.” This is Jesus’ call to everyone who follows him, and it is a key turning point in a Christian’s life. Denying yourself does not mean denying your worth. It means setting aside self-centeredness, no longer making yourself king, and letting Jesus be the Lord of your life.

The old self lives for itself, insisting on its own will, rights, and interests. The new self is willing to live for Jesus and for others, no longer only for itself. Taking up the cross does not mean treating every hardship in life as a cross. It means being willing to bear the cost of following Christ in obedience. True discipleship is more than believing that Jesus can bless me. It is being willing to hand the lordship of my life over to him, to take Jesus as my example, and to walk the road he walked.

Jesus went on: “Whoever wishes to save his life will lose it, and whoever loses his life for my sake will find it.” This seems like a paradox, yet it reveals an important principle of the gospel. The more we cling to ourselves, the more easily we lose true life. When we are willing to let go of ourselves for Christ, we find true life in him.

People think the value of life lies in how much wealth, power, status, and achievement they have. But Jesus reminds us that even if we gain the whole world, forfeiting our life profits us nothing. A self-centered life chases everything on earth, while a selfless life lets Christ be everything. Selflessness is not losing life. It is no longer letting the old self rule, so that Christ’s new life can be lived out in us. When we turn from an earthly point of view to a heavenly one, and from temporary values to eternal ones, we come to see that true abundance is not owning the whole world but gaining Jesus Christ.

Finally, Jesus points out that the Son of Man will come in the glory of his Father and will judge each person according to his deeds. This reminds us that life is not only this brief present life; it has an eternal outcome. True victory is not winning the whole world in this life, but following Christ faithfully and receiving eternal life.

We do not earn salvation by acts of self-denial. We receive Jesus and his salvation by faith, and we respond to his love with self-denial and obedience. When we let Jesus be King, with the Bible as our standard and the Holy Spirit as our guide, we move from self-centeredness to selflessness, from living for ourselves to living for Christ. Life first, then relationships, then ministry: only when Christ first changes our life can we live out his love, build relationships of unity, and fulfill the mission God has entrusted to us. This is the life of taking up the cross and following the Lord, and it is a life of victory that gives all glory to God.
a: Deny yourself daily and let Jesus be King
Set aside self-centeredness, stop insisting on your own will, rights, and interests, and learn to submit to the Lord’s will in everything.
Take up your cross and follow the Lord faithfully
Follow Jesus not only when things go well, but also be willing to pay the price for truth and love, living out the life of Christ.
Value eternity and gain true life
Do not measure life by wealth, status, and achievement. Live with an eternal perspective and let Christ be everything in your life.
q: In my life, what are the wishes, rights, interests, or pursuits that I am still holding tightly and unwilling to let go of? Am I truly willing to deny myself, take up my cross, let Jesus be King, and follow him all my life?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for giving me true life through Jesus Christ, and for calling me to deny myself, take up my cross, and follow the Lord. Shine Your light on me so that I can see the pride, self-centeredness, and craving for the world in my old self. I am willing to lay down my own will, rights, and interests, to no longer live for myself, and to let Jesus live in me and be King in me. Holy Spirit, guide me so that each day I take up my cross and faithfully obey Your will, no longer chasing the fleeting glory of the world but valuing eternal life. May I live out Christ’s humility, self-denial, and love, so that more people come to know Jesus through me, and may all glory go to You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will deny myself, take up my cross, and follow Jesus. I lay myself down for the Lord and gain true life!

t: Do Not Forget God; Turn Back and Rely on Him Alone
v: Generation, consider the LORD’s word. Have I been a wilderness to Israel? Or a land of thick darkness? Why do my people say, ‘We have broken loose. We will come to you no more’?
“Can a virgin forget her ornaments, or a bride her attire? Yet my people have forgotten me for days without number.
How well you prepare your way to seek love! Therefore you have even taught the wicked women your ways.
Also the blood of the souls of the innocent poor is found in your skirts. You didn’t find them breaking in, but it is because of all these things.
“Yet you said, ‘I am innocent. Surely his anger has turned away from me.’ “Behold, I will judge you, because you say, ‘I have not sinned.’
Why do you go about so much to change your ways? You will be ashamed of Egypt also, as you were ashamed of Assyria.
You will also leave that place with your hands on your head; for the LORD has rejected those in whom you trust, and you won’t prosper with them.
b: God rebuked the people of Israel through the prophet Jeremiah: “My people have forgotten me days without number.” God had rescued them, provided for them, and led them, yet the people gradually forgot his grace and even believed that freeing themselves from his restraints would bring them true freedom. The greatest danger for a person is not losing the blessings God gives, but receiving the blessings and then forgetting the God who gave them.

God uses the picture of a bride who would never forget her attire to show that his people had forgotten the One who matters most in their lives. We too can be so busy with work, family, daily life, and service that we neglect our close relationship with God. When people leave God and center on themselves, they easily mistake freedom for doing whatever they please. True freedom is not escaping God’s sovereignty. It is returning to our rightful place as human beings, letting God be God and letting Jesus be King in our lives.

God goes on to say that the people had not only abandoned him but had also wronged the innocent poor with injustice, yet they still claimed, “I am innocent.” This shows what is most terrible about sin: not only doing wrong, but being unwilling to admit it afterward. Pride makes us defend our mistakes. Humility makes us willing to face the truth, confess our sin, and turn back to God.

A self-centered life always tries to prove it is not at fault, shifting the blame onto others or onto circumstances. A selfless life is willing to receive the light of God’s truth and no longer covers up its sin. True repentance is more than saying with our mouth that we love God. It is letting God’s word correct our mindset, change our life, and so change the way we live and treat others. When we are willing to lay down pride, take the Bible as our standard, and be led by the Holy Spirit, we turn from self-righteousness to humble confession, and Christ’s righteousness, mercy, and love are revealed in our lives.

Finally, God rebukes the people for running here and there, seeking security by relying on Egypt and Assyria while refusing to rely wholly on him. As a result, the very things they trusted in brought them shame. True security is not finding more people, power, or resources to lean on, but relying on the one God who never changes.

When people face difficulties, they often rush to find solutions and forget to come before God first. They try to solve problems with outward means without first dealing with their inner relationship with God. God does not forbid us from accepting human help; he only asks that nothing and no one take his place. When we turn from relying on ourselves to relying on God, and from seeking the world’s security to seeking God’s will, we can rebuild a close relationship with him, let Jesus be King, live out the life of Christ, and give all glory to him.
a: Do not forget God’s grace
Count God’s guidance and provision each day, and do not let a busy life and service replace your close relationship with him.
Confess humbly and repent truly
Face your mistakes without shifting blame or defending yourself. Receive the light of God’s truth and correct your life.
Let go of other supports and trust God wholeheartedly
Do not treat money, power, connections, or your own abilities as your final security. Seek God’s will in everything and let Jesus be King.
q: Because of busyness, the pursuit of success, or reliance on my own abilities, have I gradually forgotten God’s grace? When God points out my mistakes, do I repent humbly, or do I defend myself and refuse to let Jesus be King?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You that You are a God of love and faithfulness who keeps his covenant. You have shown me so much grace in my life. Forgive me for so often remembering only my own needs and forgetting Your guidance and provision. Shine Your light on me so that I can see the pride, self-righteousness, and reliance on the world within me. I am willing to confess humbly, to lay down my claim to control, to stop defending my mistakes, and to stop relying on human ability and security, and to turn back to You wholeheartedly. Holy Spirit, guide me, and let Jesus be King in me, so that with the Bible as my standard I live out Christ’s righteousness, mercy, and love every day, rebuild a close relationship with You, and give all glory to You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will not forget God, and I will not rely on the world. I will repent humbly and turn wholeheartedly to the Lord!

t: Live a Holy Life That Pleases God
v: Finally then, brothers, we beg and exhort you in the Lord Jesus, that as you received from us how you ought to walk and to please God, that you abound more and more.
For you know what instructions we gave you through the Lord Jesus.
For this is the will of God: your sanctification, that you abstain from sexual immorality,
that each one of you know how to control his own body in sanctification and honor,
not in the passion of lust, even as the Gentiles who don’t know God,
that no one should take advantage of and wrong a brother or sister in this matter; because the Lord is an avenger in all these things, as also we forewarned you and testified.
For God called us not for uncleanness, but in sanctification.
Therefore he who rejects this doesn’t reject man, but God, who has also given his Holy Spirit to you.
But concerning brotherly love, you have no need that one write to you. For you yourselves are taught by God to love one another,
for indeed you do it toward all the brothers who are in all Macedonia. But we exhort you, brothers, that you abound more and more;
and that you make it your ambition to lead a quiet life, and to do your own business, and to work with your own hands, even as we instructed you,
that you may walk properly toward those who are outside, and may have need of nothing.
b: Paul encouraged the believers in Thessalonica that, since they already knew how to walk so as to please God, they should abound in it more and more. He then stated plainly: “This is the will of God: your sanctification.” This shows us that God calls us not only to believe in Jesus but to live out the life of Jesus.

Holiness is not an outward appearance of devotion, nor is it thinking ourselves better than others. It is being set apart from the sin of the world so that our lives truly belong to God. The old self centers on its own desires and preferences, while the new self is willing to let God’s will be the standard of life. When we turn from “How can I be happy?” to “How can I please God?”, the direction of our life begins to change. True holiness is more than staying away from sin. It is letting Jesus be King so that our thoughts, words, and actions become more and more like Christ.

Paul especially reminds believers to abstain from sexual immorality, to keep their bodies in holiness and honor, not to indulge in lustful passion, and not to overstep and wrong others. This helps us understand that true freedom is not doing whatever we want, but no longer being mastered by selfish desire and being able to live according to God’s truth.

A self-centered life thinks only of its own satisfaction and may even hurt others to gratify its desires. A selfless life respects itself and others and does not let selfish desire destroy life and relationships. God gives the Holy Spirit not so that we keep following the lusts of the old self, but to help us live in holiness by his power. When we lay down self-centeredness, let the Bible renew our mindset, and let the Holy Spirit lead our life, we turn from being controlled by selfish desire to obeying Christ, and we live out true honor and holiness in our bodies, our minds, and our relationships.

Finally, Paul extends holiness to love for one another and to everyday life. He urges believers to love one another more and more, and to aspire to live quietly, mind their own affairs, and work with their hands, so that outsiders see an upright testimony. This reminds us that a true spiritual life shows not only in worship and service at church, but also at home, at work, and in our daily lives.

A person who lets Jesus be King is not only enthusiastic about ministry. He also lives out love in his relationships, is faithful in his work, and keeps to his place in daily life. Life first, then relationships, then ministry: first let God’s truth change the inner life, then live out loving relationships from that life, and finally become a testimony that glorifies God. When we no longer seek our own performance and glory but faithfully do God’s will every day, we live out the life of Christ, and people come to know Jesus through us and give all glory to God.
a: Pursue holiness daily and please God
Do not take your own desires and preferences as the standard. Let God’s truth guide your thoughts, words, and actions.
Rely on the Holy Spirit to restrain lust and respect others
Stay away from sexual immorality and impure thoughts. Do not let selfish desire rule your life, and do not hurt others for the sake of your own needs.
Love one another and live faithfully
Live out love at home, at work, and in the church. Work quietly and responsibly, and be a beautiful testimony to the gospel.
q: Is pleasing God truly the goal of my life? In my thoughts, my body, my relationships, and my daily life, where am I still controlled by selfish desires, and where do I need to let Jesus be King and live out holiness by the Holy Spirit?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for calling me in Christ so that I no longer belong to sin but am Your holy child. Shine Your light on me so that I can see the impure thoughts, self-centeredness, and indulgence of desire in my old life. I am willing to lay myself down, no longer centering on my own desires and preferences, but letting Jesus be King in me and the Holy Spirit lead each of my days. Renew my mindset through Your truth, so that I keep my body in holiness and honor, respect others with love, and serve faithfully at home, at work, and in the church, living out the life of Christ. May my life and service please You, so that more people come to know Jesus through my testimony, and may all glory go to You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: God’s will is for me to be holy. By the Holy Spirit I will stay away from sin and love others, living a life that pleases God!

t: Do Not Wait for Judgment to Come Before Turning Back to God
v: “I struck you with blight and mildew many times in your gardens and your vineyards, and the swarming locusts have devoured your fig trees and your olive trees; yet you haven’t returned to me,” says the LORD.

“I sent plagues among you like I did Egypt. I have slain your young men with the sword, and have carried away your horses. I filled your nostrils with the stench of your camp, yet you haven’t returned to me,” says the LORD.
“I have overthrown some of you, as when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah, and you were like a burning stick plucked out of the fire; yet you haven’t returned to me,” says the LORD.
“Therefore I will do this to you, Israel; because I will do this to you, prepare to meet your God, Israel.

For, behold, he who forms the mountains, creates the wind, declares to man what is his thought, who makes the morning darkness, and treads on the high places of the earth: The LORD, the God of Armies, is his name.”
b: Through the prophet Amos, God pointed again and again to the calamities Israel had suffered and repeated, “Yet you haven’t returned to me.” This sentence exposes the people’s real spiritual crisis. The greatest crisis in life is not meeting trouble, but being unwilling to turn back to God even in trouble.

God had used various forms of discipline to remind the Israelites, hoping they would leave their sin and restore their relationship with him, yet the people’s hearts remained hard. We are often the same today. When we meet difficulties, we only want to solve the problem quickly and are unwilling to examine our own lives. We should be careful here: not every disaster is God’s punishment for the sin of the person who suffers it. But in any circumstance we can humbly seek God’s heart. True repentance is not just hoping our circumstances will change, but being willing to let God change our lives.

Though God reminded Israel again and again, they never wanted to turn back, which reveals the pride and stubbornness of the human heart. The greatest danger of pride is not only making mistakes, but still refusing to admit them after making them, and refusing to let God be King.

A self-centered life puts itself at the center of everything and insists on its own way even when reminded. A selfless life humbly receives God’s light, admits its mistakes, and submits again to his will. What God wants is not outward religious activity but a life of true repentance and obedience to the truth. When we lay down our claim to control, return to our rightful place, and let God be God, we turn from pride to humility and from rebellion to obedience. Change your mindset and your life changes; change your life and your way of living changes. True revival is not outward circumstances getting better, but human hearts turning back to God and letting Jesus be King in their lives.

Finally, God solemnly declares, “Prepare to meet your God, Israel.” This is no ordinary reminder. It is a warning of judgment to those who keep rebelling. God is the Lord of Hosts, who forms the mountains, controls the winds and clouds, and rules over all things, and no one can escape his justice. True wisdom is not to seek God only after judgment arrives, but to humbly repent and turn back to him today while there is still opportunity.

God is just, and he is also full of mercy. Through Jesus Christ he has prepared salvation for us, so that by faith we are forgiven and reconciled to him. When we are willing to leave sin, take the Bible as our standard and the Holy Spirit as our guide, and let Jesus be King, we no longer live in self-centeredness and rebellion. We live out the life of Christ and meet our God with reverence and obedience, so that all glory goes to him.
a: Accept reminders and examine yourself humbly
In difficulties and setbacks, do not only look for a solution but also examine your life by God’s truth.
Stop being hard-hearted; repent truly and turn to God
When the Bible points out your mistakes, do not make excuses or defend yourself. Lay down your pride and accept God’s correction.
Revere God and prepare to meet him
Do not put off repentance until tomorrow. Let Jesus be King every day, do God’s will, and live a holy life.
q: Has God ever shone his light on me through the truth of the Bible, through someone’s reminder, or through an experience in life, while I still insisted on my own way and refused to change? Am I truly prepared to meet God with a humble and obedient life?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You that You are the God who created heaven and earth, who rules over all things, and who is just and full of mercy. Shine Your light on me so that I can see the pride, hardness, and disobedience within me, and I will no longer take Your reminders lightly or defend my mistakes. I am willing to repent humbly, lay down my claim to control, and turn back to You. Renew my mindset through the truth of the Bible and let the Holy Spirit guide my life, so that I no longer center on myself but let Jesus live in me and be King in me. May I obey Your will every day with reverence, living out Christ’s holiness, humility, and obedience, and prepare to meet You, so that all glory goes to You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will repent humbly and turn back to the Lord, and with reverence I will prepare to meet my God!

t: Saved by Grace, Living a Renewed Life
v: For we were also once foolish, disobedient, deceived, serving various lusts and pleasures, living in malice and envy, hateful, and hating one another.
But when the kindness of God our Savior and his love toward mankind appeared,
not by works of righteousness which we did ourselves, but according to his mercy, he saved us through the washing of regeneration and renewing by the Holy Spirit,
whom he poured out on us richly through Jesus Christ our Savior;
that being justified by his grace, we might be made heirs according to the hope of eternal life.

This saying is faithful, and concerning these things I desire that you insist confidently, so that those who have believed God may be careful to maintain good works. These things are good and profitable to men;
b: Paul reminded Titus that we too were once foolish, disobedient, and deceived, ruled by all kinds of desires, and even full of envy and hatred. This shows us that the greatest problem of human beings is not merely bad outward behavior, but something wrong with the life within.

The old self centers on itself and follows its own desires in everything, wanting to get more and hold more, and in the end loses true freedom. Pride makes people leave their rightful place and want to be king themselves; self-centeredness makes people see only their own interests, ignore the needs of others, and even damage relationships. By saying “we ourselves also were once,” Paul reminds believers not to look down on others just because we have received grace, since we too once lived in sin. True humility is knowing who we really are and admitting that, without God’s grace, we could not have escaped the bondage of sin either.

Paul then declares: “Not by works of righteousness which we did ourselves, but according to his mercy, he saved us, through the washing of regeneration and renewing by the Holy Spirit.” This is the most precious truth of the gospel. Salvation is not people repairing their old life by their own effort. It is God, in his mercy, giving us new birth and a brand-new life.

We are not rescued by God because we are good enough. We are rescued because God loves us, accomplishes salvation through Jesus Christ, and pours out the Holy Spirit richly on us, so that our life is continually renewed. Regeneration is the new life God gives, and renewal is that new life gradually shown in daily living. Selflessness is not becoming better by our own effort; it is no longer letting the old self rule and letting Christ live in us. When we take the Bible as our standard and the Holy Spirit as our guide, we turn from self-centeredness to selflessness, and from being controlled by selfish desire to letting Jesus be King.

Finally, Paul points out that we are justified by God’s grace and made heirs of the hope of eternal life, and so we should be careful to do good, bringing benefit to others. This helps us understand that we do not do good to buy salvation; we live out a new life of doing good because we have already been saved by grace.

The gospel changes not only our standing before God but also our daily life. In the past we centered on ourselves; now we center on Christ. In the past we cared only about our own interests; now we are willing to be a blessing to others. In the past we were bound by envy and hatred; now by the Holy Spirit we live out humility and love. Change your mindset and your life changes; change your life and your way of living changes. Life first, then relationships, then ministry: when God’s grace truly renews our life, we can build good relationships and live in a way that glorifies God and builds up others, so that more people come to know Jesus through us.
a: Remember grace and keep a humble heart
Never forget that you too are a sinner saved by grace. Do not become proud over others’ weaknesses, but learn to treat people with mercy and love.
Be renewed daily by the Holy Spirit
Stop following the desires and self-centeredness of the old self. Let the truth of the Bible change your mindset and let Jesus be King in your life.
Saved by grace, careful to do good
Do not leave your faith at the level of knowledge and words. Take the initiative to care for, serve, and bless others, so that they are helped.
q: Do I truly understand that my salvation is entirely by God’s grace? Which thoughts, attitudes, and habits of the old self in my life today need the Holy Spirit’s renewal, so that I can live out Christ and be a blessing to others?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for saving me with Your abundant kindness and mercy, so that I am justified not by my own righteousness but through the salvation of Jesus Christ, and receive the life of regeneration and the hope of eternal life. Help me never to forget who I really am, and remove the pride, self-centeredness, envy, and selfish desire within me. I am willing to lay myself down, no longer letting the old self rule, but letting Jesus live in me and be King in me. Holy Spirit, renew my mindset, my life, and my way of living every day, so that I am not only saved by grace but also live out Christ’s humility, kindness, and goodness, careful to do good and be a blessing to others, so that all glory goes to You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I am saved not by my own righteousness but by God’s mercy. By the Holy Spirit I will renew my life, be careful to do good, and live out the hope of eternal life!

t: Look to God’s Provision and Praise Him All Your Life
v: LORD, how many are your works! In wisdom, you have made them all. The earth is full of your riches.
There is the sea, great and wide, in which are innumerable living things, both small and large animals.
There the ships go, and leviathan, whom you formed to play there.
These all wait for you, that you may give them their food in due season.
You give to them; they gather. You open your hand; they are satisfied with good.
You hide your face; they are troubled. You take away their breath; they die and return to the dust.
You send out your Spirit and they are created. You renew the face of the ground.
Let the LORD’s glory endure forever. Let the LORD rejoice in his works.
He looks at the earth, and it trembles. He touches the mountains, and they smoke.
I will sing to the LORD as long as I live. I will sing praise to my God while I have any being.
Let my meditation be sweet to him. I will rejoice in the LORD.
b: The psalmist looks up at heaven, earth, and all creation and cannot help exclaiming, “Lord, how many are your works! In wisdom you have made them all. The earth is full of your riches.” From the vast ocean to its countless creatures, from the tiniest life to the greatest living things, everything displays the wisdom and abundance of God’s creation. True wisdom is not that the more we know, the greater we become, but that the more we know of creation, the more humbly we revere the Creator.

People often become proud of their knowledge, abilities, and achievements and forget that they too are created by God. When we turn from the human point of view to God’s point of view, we see that the world does not center on me, and that life is not for displaying my own glory. Humility is returning to our rightful place as human beings and admitting that God is the Lord who created all things. When we lay down self-centeredness and let Jesus be King, we move from admiring God’s creation to knowing his wisdom, power, and glory more deeply.

The psalmist goes on to say that all living things look to God to give them food in due season: when God opens his hand they are satisfied, when he takes away their breath they return to dust, and when he sends out his Spirit the ground is renewed. This shows us that life is not sustained by ourselves but depends moment by moment on God’s provision and care.

People think they can control their lives and secure their future by effort, wealth, and ability, forgetting that even the breath in their lungs is a gift from God. We can work hard, but we cannot create life; we can accumulate resources, but we cannot govern tomorrow. True faith does not mean doing nothing. It means being faithful in our duties while admitting that everything needs God’s grace. When we no longer rely on our own ability but look to God alone, we learn contentment, thanksgiving, and entrusting ourselves to him, and we let the Holy Spirit lead our daily life so that our life is continually renewed by him.

Finally, the psalmist declares, “I will sing to the Lord as long as I live. I will sing praise to my God while I have any being.” When he sees the wisdom of God’s creation, the grace of his provision, and the power of his rule, he no longer fixes his eyes on himself but resolves to praise God all his life. True worship is more than singing with our mouths. It is letting our whole life become praise that glorifies God.

God deserves not only our singing at gatherings but also our thoughts, words, actions, and daily life. When we take the Bible as our standard and the Holy Spirit as our guide, and let Jesus live and be King within us, we turn from living for ourselves to living for God. Even when circumstances change, we still remember his grace; even when we face difficulties, we still trust his provision. May we not only receive God’s abundance all our lives but also become children who please him, so that all glory goes to him.
a: Admire creation and revere God humbly
From the heavens and earth you see every day, meditate on God’s wisdom and power, and do not become proud of your knowledge and achievements.
Look to God’s provision every day
Do not treat your own ability and wealth as the security of your life. Learn thankfulness and contentment, and trust God’s leading in everything.
Live a life of praising God
Praise God not only in worship, but let your thoughts, words, life, and service all please him and give the glory to him.
q: Do I truly understand that my life, my breath, and everything that supplies my needs come from God? Do I live each day relying on my own ability, or do I look to God with a thankful heart and let my whole life become a testimony of praise to him?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You that You are the God who created heaven, earth, and all things, full of wisdom and abundance. Everything You have made displays Your glory, and You supply the needs of all creatures in due season. Remove the pride and self-centeredness within me, so that I no longer rely on my own cleverness, ability, and wealth, but humbly admit that everything in my life comes from You. I am willing to lay myself down and let Jesus be King in me, and let the Holy Spirit renew and guide my life every day. Help me not only to receive Your grace but also to live out the life of Christ with a thankful heart, so that my thoughts, words, life, and service become praise that pleases You, and all glory goes to You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will sing to the Lord all my life, look to his provision every day, and rejoice in him, so that his glory endures forever!

t: Let Your Heart Be Good Soil and Bear Abundant Fruit
v: On that day Jesus went out of the house and sat by the seaside.
Great multitudes gathered to him, so that he entered into a boat and sat; and all the multitude stood on the beach.
He spoke to them many things in parables, saying, “Behold, a farmer went out to sow.
As he sowed, some seeds fell by the roadside, and the birds came and devoured them.
Others fell on rocky ground, where they didn’t have much soil, and immediately they sprang up, because they had no depth of earth.
When the sun had risen, they were scorched. Because they had no root, they withered away.
Others fell among thorns. The thorns grew up and choked them.
Others fell on good soil and yielded fruit: some one hundred times as much, some sixty, and some thirty.
He who has ears to hear, let him hear.”
b: Jesus uses the parable of the sower to show the different ways people respond to God’s word. The seed stands for the word of God, and the four kinds of soil reflect the different conditions of human hearts. The hard path keeps the seed from going deep, and the rocky ground sprouts quickly but withers because it has no root. True hearing is more than ears hearing the truth. It is letting the truth enter the heart and change one’s own life.

People often hear many teachings but do not truly receive them, because their hearts are still full of their own ideas, pride, and stubbornness. A self-centered life likes to choose what it wants to hear and is unwilling to accept God’s reminders and corrections, while a humble life opens the door of the heart and lets God’s word take root. When we lay down our claim to control, take the Bible as our standard, and let Jesus be King in our lives, God’s truth can move from information into life and become a power that truly changes us.

Jesus then speaks of the seed that fell among thorns, which began to grow but was choked by the thorns and could not bear fruit. Jesus later explained that the thorns are the cares of the world and the deceitfulness of riches, which keep God’s word from bearing fruit. The greatest danger to our life is not necessarily rejecting God’s word, but accepting the truth while the heart is filled with the world, leaving no room for God to be King.

We may read the Bible, pray, and attend gatherings every day, yet still be pulled along by money, achievement, power, and our own desires, so that the truth stays in the head and never changes our life. Change your mindset and your life changes; change your life and your way of living changes. When we no longer center on ourselves and let the Holy Spirit shine his light and remove the thorns in our hearts, we turn from an earthly point of view to a heavenly one, and from temporary pursuits to eternal values, so that Christ’s life can grow freely within us.

Finally, Jesus says that the seed that fell on good soil bore thirty, sixty, even a hundred times as much. Good soil is not ground that never had stones or weeds. It is ground willing to be prepared, so that the seed can take root, grow, and bear fruit. A truly abundant life is not about how many Bible teachings we know, but about how much truth has become our own life and way of living.

When we are willing to receive God’s word humbly and let the Holy Spirit continually renew our mindset and correct our lives, we gradually live out Christ’s humility, love, holiness, and obedience. What God values is not only how much ministry we do, but whether our life truly bears fruit. Life first, then relationships, then ministry: when truth first changes our inner life, we can live out loving relationships outwardly and become vessels that bless others. Let Jesus be King, and our lives will naturally bear fruit that glorifies God.
a: Remove hardness and pride from your heart
When you hear God’s word, do not accept only the parts you like, but humbly receive the truth’s reminders and corrections.
Pull out the thorns of worldly cares
Do not let money, achievement, and the worries of life occupy your heart. Learn to keep your focus on Jesus.
Let truth take root and live an abundant life
Do not only read the Bible and hear sermons, but put them into practice every day, so that God’s word changes your mindset, life, way of living, and relationships.
q: Is my heart right now the hard path, the rocky ground with no root, the soil full of thorns, or the good soil willing to be changed by God’s truth and bear abundant fruit? Which stone or which patch of thorns do I most need to remove?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for giving me the truth of life through Jesus Christ. Shine Your light into my heart so that I can see the pride, hardness, worry, and deception of the world within me, and no longer let them keep Your word from taking root in my life. I am willing to lay myself down and let Jesus be King in me, and let the Holy Spirit prepare my heart, so that I become good soil that is humble, soft, and willing to obey the truth. Help me not only to hear but to do, not only to gain knowledge but to change my life. May Your word take deep root in me, so that I live out Christ’s humility, love, and holiness, and my life, relationships, and service bear abundant fruit, giving all glory to You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will be good soil that receives God’s truth, let his word take deep root, and bear thirty, sixty, and a hundred times as much fruit!

t: Guard Your Heart and Live a Life of Victory
v: My son, attend to my words. Turn your ear to my sayings.
Let them not depart from your eyes. Keep them in the center of your heart.
For they are life to those who find them, and health to their whole body.
Keep your heart with all diligence, for out of it is the wellspring of life.
Put away from yourself a perverse mouth. Put corrupt lips far from you.
Let your eyes look straight ahead. Fix your gaze directly before you.
Make the path of your feet level. Let all of your ways be established.
Don’t turn to the right hand nor to the left. Remove your foot from evil.
b: Proverbs reminds us, “Attend to my words… keep them in the center of your heart.” This shows us that God’s truth is not only to increase our knowledge but to enter our hearts and become the standard of our lives. True wisdom is not how many teachings the head understands, but how much truth the heart receives and is willing to obey.

People often hear many sermons and know what is right, yet their lives do not change, because the truth stays at the level of knowledge and never truly enters life. God’s word is life-giving medicine. It can shine on our wrong mindset, heal the damage sin has done, and lead us on the path of life. When we no longer rely on our own cleverness but take the Bible as our standard and let the Holy Spirit guide us, we turn from the human point of view to God’s point of view, so that truth is not only what we know but what we live out.

The most important reminder in this passage is: “Guard your heart with all diligence, for out of it is the wellspring of life.” The heart is the center of life, and who reigns in the heart determines what kind of life we live out.

People take great care to protect their possessions, health, status, and relationships, yet neglect to guard their hearts. When the heart is full of pride, envy, greed, and self-centeredness, our words and actions easily hurt others; when the heart is full of God’s truth, love, humility, and holiness, our life naturally shows the goodness of Christ. A self-centered life lets its own desires and emotions be king, while a selfless life is willing to lay itself down and let Jesus live and be King within. Change your mindset and your life changes; change your life and your way of living changes. True change is not first polishing outward behavior, but letting the Holy Spirit renew us from the heart, so that life changes from the inside out.

Finally, Proverbs teaches us to put away a deceitful mouth, to look straight ahead, to make level the path of our feet, and not to turn to the right or the left. This shows us that guarding our hearts must be carried out in our words, our gaze, and our actions.

What the heart thinks affects what the mouth says; what the eyes fix on affects the direction of life’s pursuits; the steps our feet choose determine where our life goes. When we focus on ourselves, others, or circumstances, we are easily pulled by pride, comparison, and worry; but when we fix our eyes on Jesus, we no longer stray from God’s path. True victory is not only overcoming outward difficulties but guarding our hearts by the Holy Spirit, so that our thoughts, words, life, and actions all obey Christ. When Jesus becomes the focus of everything, his life can be lived out through us, and the outcome of our whole life becomes a beautiful testimony that glorifies God and blesses others.
a: Receive truth daily and guard your heart
Do not let God’s word stay in your head. Keep it in your heart and let truth renew your mindset and change your life.
Let Jesus be King over your thoughts and words
Do not let pride, emotions, and selfish desire rule your heart. By the Holy Spirit, live out humility, love, and holiness.
Fix your eyes on Jesus and walk the upright path
Do not be pulled by others, circumstances, or the world’s values. Take the Bible as your standard and firmly obey God’s will.
q: Who is king over my heart right now? My own emotions, desires, pride, and worries, or Jesus Christ? Am I truly guarding my heart and letting God’s truth decide my thoughts, my words, and the direction of my life?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for the precious truth that gives me life, and for helping me understand that the outcome of my whole life flows from the heart. Shine Your light into my heart so that I can see the pride, self-centeredness, selfish desire, and worry within me, and no longer let them rule my life. I am willing to lay myself down and let Jesus live in me and be King in me. Holy Spirit, guide me so that I guard my heart every day, keep Your word deep in my heart, and let it renew my mindset, my life, and my way of living. Keep my mouth from evil words, keep my eyes fixed on Jesus, and keep my steps on the upright path, so that all my life I do not stray from Your will, but live out the life of Christ and give all glory to You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will guard my heart above all else and fix my eyes on Jesus, for the outcome of my whole life flows from the heart!

t: Live a Holy Life and Treat Others with Love and Justice
v: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
“Speak to all the congregation of the children of Israel, and tell them, ‘You shall be holy; for I, the LORD your God, am holy.
“‘If a stranger lives as a foreigner with you in your land, you shall not do him wrong.

The stranger who lives as a foreigner with you shall be to you as the native-born among you, and you shall love him as yourself; for you lived as foreigners in the land of Egypt. I am the LORD your God.
“‘You shall do no unrighteousness in judgment, in measures of length, of weight, or of quantity.
You shall have just balances, just weights, a just ephah, and a just hin. I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt.
“‘You shall observe all my statutes and all my ordinances, and do them. I am the LORD.’”
b: God commanded the people of Israel, “You shall be holy; for I the Lord your God am holy.” This shows us that holiness is not devotion displayed only in religious activities, but living out God’s character in everyday life.

God is holy, and he calls those who belong to him to be set apart, showing his beauty in their thoughts, words, actions, and relationships. People often think holiness means staying away from the world and doing nothing wrong, but the holiness God asks for is not only passively leaving sin but actively living out justice, mercy, and love. True change of life does not come from polishing our behavior with outward rules, but from God’s truth renewing our mindset and the Holy Spirit changing our life, so that Christ’s character is lived out from within. When we no longer center on ourselves and let Jesus be King, holiness is no longer only a doctrine we know but a life we live out every day.

God then commands the people not to mistreat the foreigners who live among them, but to treat them as the native-born and to love them as themselves. God especially reminds Israel, “For you were strangers in the land of Egypt.” True love is not only being kind to people like ourselves, but being willing to accept, respect, and care for those who are different from us.

The old self easily centers on its own identity, status, and interests, drawing close to the familiar and keeping distance from strangers, and even looking down on others because of differences. But God wants us to remember the grace we ourselves have received and to treat those in need with compassion. A self-centered life guards only its own rights; a selfless life is willing to lay down its sense of superiority and learn to treat others kindly with Christ’s love. People matter more than things, and relationships matter more than possessions. When we take Jesus as our example, we can cross differences of status and background, so that more people experience God’s love through us.

Finally, God commands the people not to act unjustly in judgment or in trade, but to use just balances, weights, and measures. This helps us understand that true holiness shows not only when we worship God, but also in whether we remain honest, fair, and upright where no one is watching.

A person may seem devout at church yet lose justice at work, in money matters, and in relationships for the sake of personal gain. God does not want us to live by two sets of standards; he wants truth to run through every part of our lives. Change your mindset and your life changes; change your life and your way of living changes. When we take the Bible as our standard and the Holy Spirit as our guide, and let Jesus live and be King within us, we turn from pursuing our own interests to doing God’s will, living out love at home, integrity at work, and justice in relationships, so that our whole life becomes a testimony that glorifies God.
a: Pursue holiness and live out the life of Christ
Be devout not only in worship and service, but let God’s truth change your thoughts, words, and actions each day.
Love others as yourself and care for those who are different
Do not look down on others because of differences in status, background, or circumstances. Take the initiative to respect, accept, and help those in need.
Be honest and just, pleasing God in everything
At work, in money matters, and in relationships, hold to honesty and fairness, and do not sacrifice others’ rights for your own gain.
q: Does my holiness show only in worship and service at church, or is it truly carried out in how I treat people, in my work, my money, and every detail of my life? Am I willing to let Jesus be King and live out God’s justice and love?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You that You are holy, just, and full of love. You call me to be holy because You are holy. Shine Your light on me so that I can see the pride, selfishness, prejudice, and injustice within me, and I will no longer pursue only outward devotion but let Your truth truly change my life. I am willing to lay myself down and let Jesus live in me and be King in me, and let the Holy Spirit guide each of my days. Help me learn to treat others with Christ’s love, so that regardless of status or background I respect, accept, care for, and bless them. At work, with money, and in daily life, help me hold to honesty, fairness, and uprightness, living out Christ’s holiness, justice, and love, so that all glory goes to You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will be holy, because my God is holy. I will love others as myself, act justly, and keep and do God’s word!
